claim: Modern product strategy is shaped via lightweight mechanisms: working-backwards (Amazon), PR/FAQ, continuous discovery (Teresa Torres), and Shape Up. Heavy stage-gate portfolio governance is deprecated.
Outcome-based OKRs and product OKR alignment are the canonical strategy-execution model. Teams set objectives, but rollup to organizational OKRs is lightweight, not waterfall.
Continuous Discovery (Teresa Torres) and Shape Up shaping are convergent: the product team talks to users weekly, runs opportunity solution trees, and shapes work before committing to a cycle.
User stories are a lightweight contract, not a detailed specification. Story Mapping (Patton) is the canonical approach for backlog organization.
Google HEART (Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task success) is the canonical user-experience metric framework.
Three cloud providers' Well-Architected frameworks (Google, Microsoft, AWS) converge on the same five pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost optimization.
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and lightweight RFC culture are the canonical documentation practice. Big-design-up-front is deprecated.
Microservices are defined by independent deployability, business-capability alignment, decentralized data, smart endpoints and dumb pipes (Fowler/Lewis 2014).
Evolutionary architecture and fitness functions are the canonical way to govern long-lived systems; strangler fig for incremental migration of legacy.
Trunk-based development is the canonical branching model for high-performing teams; short-lived branches (<= 2 days) and feature flags are the supporting mechanisms.
Shape Up's 6-week building cycle, shaping-before-betting, and cooling periods are the canonical lightweight planning cadence.
Backlog management is a JIT (just-in-time) practice, not a stockpile: only work that is shaped and ready enters the build cycle.
Cloud-based dev environments (GitHub Codespaces, Gitpod) and standardized devcontainers are the canonical local-to-remote dev environment pattern in 2026.
Large monorepos with remote build caching (Bazel, Pants, Nx) are the canonical build system for monorepo orgs; trunk-based development enables this.
InnerSource and CONTRIBUTING.md standards are the canonical patterns for cross-team contribution in large monorepos.
Feature flags separate release from deployment; toggles have a lifecycle (release, experiment, ops, permission).
Semantic versioning and conventional commits are the canonical change-discipline patterns for libraries and APIs.
Code review is a primary knowledge-sharing mechanism; small CLs (Google), review ownership by the author, and positive culture are canonical.
Conventional Comments and PR templates are the canonical light-weight structures for code review; heavyweight governance review boards are deprecated.
Test pyramid: many unit tests, fewer integration, fewer contract, few E2E; shift-left with TDD/BDD; exploratory testing by humans.
Contract testing (Pact) is the canonical pattern for service-to-service API testing in microservice architectures.
Property-based testing, mutation testing, and fuzz testing are emerging as the canonical augmentation to example-based unit tests.
Hermetic, reproducible, content-addressed builds (Bazel) are the canonical build pattern; OCI artifacts and SLSA L3 provenance are the canonical supply chain integrity standard.
Software Bill of Materials (SBOM, CycloneDX/SPDX) is the canonical artifact metadata for compliance and vulnerability response.
Continuous Delivery: trunk always deployable, automated pipeline, on-demand deploy, separate release from deployment.
Progressive delivery: canary releases, blue-green, and feature flags are the canonical safe-rollout mechanisms.
GitOps (declarative configuration in git, automatic reconciliation) is the canonical operational model for Kubernetes and beyond.
DORA's four key metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change fail rate, MTTR) are the canonical delivery-performance measurements.
Platform engineering team is a first-class organizational pattern; stream-aligned, enabling, complicated-subsystem, and platform teams are the four canonical team types.
Internal Developer Portals (Backstage) and golden paths are the canonical interface between platform team and stream-aligned teams.
IDPs are built and operated as products: with product management, customer research (of internal users), roadmaps, and SLOs.
NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) is the canonical US-government-aligned secure SDLC framework; OWASP SAMM is the canonical software assurance maturity model.
Threat modeling (STRIDE, PASTA), SAST/DAST/SCA in CI, secrets management, signed commits, SBOM, and SLSA provenance are the canonical security controls.
Shift-left security: security testing happens during implementation, not after. DevSecOps is the canonical model, not bolt-on QA at release.
SRE: SLOs, error budgets, toil elimination (target <50%), on-call practices, blameless postmortems, automation. Embracing risk is foundational.
Chaos engineering: experimentally verify system resilience by injecting failures; Netflix's Principles of Chaos are canonical.
Incident management: severity levels, incident commander, communication cadence, postmortem within 5 business days, follow-up action items with owners.
Observability = traces + metrics + logs (the three pillars), enabled by OpenTelemetry as the canonical instrumentation standard.
RED method (Rate, Errors, Duration) for services; USE method (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) for resources. Both canonical, complementary.
Structured logs, distributed tracing, and high-cardinality metrics are the canonical observability data shapes. Sampling is essential at scale.
DORA four keys + SPACE (Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication, Efficiency) + DevEx quadrant are the canonical developer productivity measurement frameworks.
Vanity metrics (lines of code, story points) are deprecated; outcome-based metrics (cycle time, on-call load, system reliability) are canonical.
Deprecation policy: version N-1 supported, advance notice, sunset headers, migration guides, in-app warnings, end-of-life calendar published.
Legacy modernization: strangler fig, branch by abstraction, event-driven decoupling; big-bang rewrites are deprecated.
AI code assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex) are operationally adopted at scale in 2026; 55% faster on coding tasks per GitHub/Accenture study.
Agentic coding (Anthropic Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Jules, Cognition Devin) is the emerging pattern; explore-plan-implement loop and context management are canonical patterns.
Anthropic's workflow patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer. Agents use tool feedback in a loop.
SWE-bench / SWE-bench Verified is the canonical benchmark for AI software engineering agents.
NIST has published SSDF Community Profile for GenAI / foundation models (SP 800-218A); enterprise AI governance is converging on this.
AI-assisted code review, AI-generated tests, AI observability analysis, and AI incident response are emerging operational practices with credible adoption evidence.
